Commentary.Commentary: The players are back out in the field. India Women will be happy with the target of 220 which definitely looks chaseable. But there is a caveat to this - the batting could be tricky and it certainly is not easy to go at 6-an-over. Having said that, this is India's best chance in this tour. Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana are the openers for India Women. Katherine Brunt will start off proceedings to Shafali. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

220 to win then. This is those in-between targets which sometimes creates confusion in the minds of the batters regarding the approach. Should they attack? Should they preserve their wickets? This is a tricky pitch and batting looks difficult. In such scenarios, the batting of Shafali Verma could be highly crucial. A good start against the new balls could set the tone. Stay tuned for the run chase...

Spectacular bowling and fielding from India Women. They were on the money right from the start. A bit of criticism can be given to them for not quite stopping the singles in the middle overs and allowing England to get away but the visitors came back superbly in the end. Deepti Sharma was the pick of the bowlers with a 3-fer but everyone else was economical.

After being put in, England struggled early on, losing Tammy Beaumont cheaply. But Lauren Winfield, skipper Heather Knight and Natalie Sciver put the pressure back on the visitors with back-to-back decent stands. Things were going along nicely, with England at 151/3 in the 34th over. Base set for a final flourish where they would have expected another 100 runs at least. But Jones' wicket triggered a collapse and very much like what happened to India in the first two ODIs, the cat was set free amongst the pigeons, before Sophia Dunkley and Kate Cross ensured that the hosts at least played out their 47 overs.

A good flourish from England Women at the end. 22 runs came in the last 2 overs and that has given their score a competitive edge. But by no means, is it matchwinning. They were going for a score well beyond 250 but have floundered their good foundation.

OUT! A run out to end the innings. England finish on a competitive 219. Full, around middle, Kate Cross comes down the track and hammers it to long on. Radha Yadav, the subsitute, collects it easily over there and the batters actually start running the second when the throw is being released. Easy run out at the bowler's end.
Commentary.Howout: run out (sub Radha Yadav / Deepti Sharma)

Commentary.Commentary: Full, around off, Kate slogs this towards deep mid-wicket. Sneh Rana fumbles a touch at the boundary and the batters return for the second. The throw comes to the bowler who has a shy at her end and appeals but Glenn is well in.

SIX! What was Shafali Verma doing 10 yards inside the circle? Full, outside off, Cross comes down the track and swings it towards long off. Should have been an easy catch but for some reason, Shafali is standing way too in. The ball lobs up over her and clears the ropes. Had she been at the ropes, it would have been a sitter!
FOUR! This time, she connects. Full, around middle, Kate Cross comes down the track and powers this through long on, beating the fielder to her left.
Another dot. Again, Cross comes down the track, swings hard, but gets it off the inner half of the bat, back to the bowler.
Looped up, slower through the air, around middle, Kate Cross comes down the track and swings hard but gets it off the inner half of the bat towards short mid-wicket.
FOUR! Outside off, on a length, Glenn makes use of the field being brought up and lofts this over cover. Jhulan Goswami finishes with figures of 9-0-31-1.
JUST CLEARS MID OFF. Full, around off, Glenn looks to go big down the ground but gets a top edge. Clears mid off running back. Two runs taken.
Around middle, Sarah Glenn swings it straight to short mid-wicket.
200 UP FOR ENGLAND! It has been a real struggle. Full, around middle and leg, Cross looks to flick but gets it off her pads to fine leg, taking a leg bye.
Just over! Full, outside off, Kate Cross slices this over a leaping point fielder for a couple of runs.
Full, around off, driven straight to mid off.
Quicker one, outside off, Glenn looks to cut but misses. 5 runs and 2 wickets from the over, Deepti's figures read 9-0-34-3!

Deepti does really well to get across to her right to stop the ball. But poor old Shrubsole is looking for the single and is backing up too far! Sharma gathers the ball and throws it onto the stumps.

Comes down the track, is not to the pitch of the ball and pushes the ball back to the boler.

The umpire agrees and Ecclestone decides to review. Ball Tracker shows it to be clipping the outer half of leg stump but that will do for the decision to stay! England in danger of being bowled out.
The third umpire into play again! This time for DRS. Sophie Ecclestone has been adjudged LBW and she has decided to challenge it. Looks to be clipping leg. UMPIRE'S CALL, BY JUST!

Is that a run out? Mithali Raj has produced a direct hit at the bowler's end. Referred upstairs. Nope. Dunkley is well in.

OUT! CAUGHT THIS TIME! Poor, poor cricket from Lauren Winfield. Just a ball ago, she had seen her skipper almost lose her wicket playing an exact similar shot but Winfield does not learn. The ball is tossed up, outside off and Lauren gets down to play the slog sweep. She hits it with more power than her skipper but she thinks she has covered the large outfield. No, she has not. Deep mid-wicket does not have to move an inch and Shikha Pandey takes a dolly. Rana has her arms aloft and sports a wide smile. Right into the trap. A wicket gifted away but India will not care. The 67-run stand has been broken.
Commentary.Howout: c Shikha Pandey b Sneh Rana

It reads 60 as of now and is going at a rate of above 4. India Women have not done much badly but they perhaps need to choke the run flow. Too many easy singles are on offer at the moment.

Around off, nudged to the leg side.
Nice drve to finish but it is pretty much the same. Frustration continues for the English opener. Full, around off, driven straight to mid on.
Outside off, on a length, punched straight to cover. Winfield is getting a little frustrated now. India are not giving anything away.
That is the one which goes the other way. Outside off, on a length, Knight steers it behind point for a single.
Ooohh... short again, around middle, this time Winfield pulls it uppishly. Almost holes out to Jhulan Goswami at deep fine leg. Lands just short. A single taken.
Opportunity missed. Short and down the leg side, Lauren Winfield looks to pull but misses. WIDE signalled.
Similar ball, around off, driven back to Shikha Pandey again.
Full, outside off, nice shape, swinging back in, driven back to the bowler.
On a good length, outside off, blocked towards cover.
Outside off, pushed to the off side.

Good footwork by Shikha Pandey. A length ball, a bit too straight, Heather Knight clips it behind square leg. Pandey is not the quickest on the field but she gets to the ball by jogging to her left from long leg, careful not to slip. Stops the ball with her foot and the batters take two.
Landed outside off, driven straight to cover.
Fullish, around off, clipped towards short mid-wicket.
Outside off, pushed towards cover.
Around off, skidding back in, Lauren looks to flick but misses and is hit on the pads.

WIDE BUT WHAT EXCELLENT GLOVEWORK. Kudos to Taniya Bhatia. She is upto the stumps and Pandey bowls it down the leg side. Winfield misses her flick and is out of her crease. Bhatia gets down to her left, collects the ball and has a flick at the keeper's end. Hits the stumps and the stumping appeal is referred upstairs. Replays show that the batter is safe.
Around off, nudged to the leg side.
Fullish, outside off, defended watchfully.
Around off, pushed towrads mid on.
FOUR! Lovely shot. Outside off, on a length, Winfield backs away and lofts it over cover.
Full, down the leg side, Lauren Winfield misses her flick and is hit on the pads.
Full, outside off, pushed towards cover.
Around off, pushed towards mid on.
A dot on the Free Hit. Outside off, on a length, stays low, Winfield looks to drive but misses. The keeper is upto the stumps, looks to stop the ball, but is hit hard on the gloves. Ouch.

FOUR! That is a hack. Not too much wrong done by the bowler there. Lauren Winfield tries to force the pace. Comes down the track but is not to the pitch of the ball. Swings hard and gets it off the inner half of the bat, wide of mid on. That ball was bowled at a good length but the discipline is not good! The third umpire signals it a NO BALL FOR FRONT FOOT OVERSTEPPING and the on-field umpire shows it to the players! Free Hit coming up...
This one keeps low from a good length, outside off, Winfield pushes it towards point.
Outside off, on a length, holds off the surface, Lauren Winfield looks to punch it through the off side but the ball comes on slowly and goes off the inner half of the bat towards mid on.
Fuller, just around off, watchfully defended.
Better from the bowler. Full, just around off, watchfully defended. 4 runs and a wicket from the over.
FOUR! Kind bowler New batter and what does the new-ball bowler do? Gift her a present. Short and wide outside off, Heather Knight gets across and punches it through the covers. Off the mark in style.
England skipper, Heather Knight, walks out at number 3, replacing Tammy Beaumont.

OUT! LBW! That is a grubber, to be honest. Really unlucky. You pull on this wicket at your own peril. On a length, outside off, Tammy Beaumont looks to pull but the ball shoots low and goes beneath the bat. Hits her just above the knee roll and that looks like a dead duck. Does not even bother to review when the umpire upholds the Indians' appeal. This has been an excellent start from India.
Around off, on a length, solidly defended.
Outside off, on a length, punched towards cover again.
Short to start, outside off, Tammy Beaumont punches it straight to cover.
Shikha Pandey to bowl with the second new ball.
Good shot and a good stop to end the over. Half volley outside off, Lauren drives through cover-point but Smriti Mandhana does well at point.
Outside off, punched towards cover.
LBW shouts, turned down. A length ball, outside off, coming in, Lauren Winfield misses her tuck and is hit on the pads. Looked to be high and going down the leg side as well.
Excellent fielding. Fullish, outside off, LW drives through the covers but Jemimah Rodrigues dives to her left to stop. Winfield wanted a run but is sent back.
This one stays low, outside off, pitching on a good length, Lauren gets her bat down in time to defend.
Fuller, wider outside off, but well inside the wide guideline, let through again.
A wide to start. A length ball, down the leg side, Lauren Winfield lets it go.

Right then. We are all set to begin. The conditions are overcast but much brighter than what they were a couple of hours ago. The Indian players are out in a huddle and disperse after a pep talk. Out come the two English openers - Tammy Beaumont and Lauren Winfield. Punch of the fists, a smile and off they go. Aha.. the weather smiles as well, with the sun peeking out. Nice. Jhulan Goswami will start off proceedings with the ball. Lauren Winfield to face. Here we go... The 47-over-a-side contest is about to start...

ENGLAND WOMEN (UNCHANGED PLAYING XI) - Lauren Winfield, Tammy Beaumont, Heather Knight (C), Natalie Sciver, Amy Jones (WK), Sophia Dunkley, Katherine Brunt, Sophie Ecclestone, Sarah Glenn, Anya Shrubsole and Kate Cross.

INDIA WOMEN (UNCHANGED PLAYING XI) - Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Jemimah Rodrigues, Mithali Raj (C), Harmanpreet Kaur, Deepti Sharma, Sneh Rana, Taniya Bhatia (WK), Shikha Pandey, Jhulan Goswami and Poonam Yadav.
TOSS TIME! This time it is for actual. Mithali Raj has called correctly and INDIA WOMEN CHOOSE TO CHASE. Both sides are unchanged from their last game.
GAME TO START AT 12.30 pm LOCAL! That is at 1130 GMT. Because of the 90-minute delay, we have lost 6 overs. It will be a 47-over-a-side contest.
Meanwhile, the SUN IS OUT at Worcester. That is good news. Will help in quick drying of the outfield. Drying the outfield is never a problem in England but they can always use the extra help.

Take care, Chinelle Henry and Chidean Nation. News is coming from that part of the world, i.e., West Indies, that these two women collapsed during the second T20I against Pakistan last night, in two separate incidents. Both were taken to the hospital and the West Indies Cricket Board has tweeted that both are conscious and stable. Phew. Other players confirmed that the conditions were definitely challenging for the players. Wish them speedy recovery.

DROPPED! Huh? No, the game has not started yet. But just was having a look at the highlights package from the second ODI. England dropped a sitter of Shafali Verma during Powerplay 1 and catching is something which has been plaguing them right from the start of the tour. They should have won the one-off Test, but for some really sloppy fielding and that has been haunting them in the ODIs as well. With the wet ball today, their catching and fielding will be tested even more.

TOSS TIME! No, not yet. The covers continue to be placed at Worcester, though the news filtering in is that the rain has stopped. The umpires will carry out an inspection at 11.15 am local (1015 GMT). The conditions look very gloomy as well.

What is special about 3rd July? Ummm... perhaps a day before the American Independence Day? Ahhh... let's stick to sport. It is a big day for Sophie Ecclestone. On this day, in 2016, Ecclestone made her international debut, in the 1st T20I against Pakistan, in Bristol. Finished with respectable figures of 4-0-21-1. Has taken the world by storm since. Today though, might be challenging for her, given the conditions. But happy 5 years of international cricket, Sophie!
IN FOR A DELAY? BCCI has just tweeted that the ground at Worcester is covered and it does not look good at all. This was around an hour ago. Let's hope for some positive news.
However, in some good news for India, skipper Mithali Raj is all set to play today. The captain had some issues with her neck during the second ODI and was off the field. She seems to have recovered.

A bit of bad news first up. There is plenty of rain forecast during the game but if the met department is to be believed, the heavens will start opening up within an hour of the commencement of the game. The skies will stay overcast, so swing bowling will be aided. Regardless to say, looking at the conditions and the possible prospect of a start-stop contest, fielding first would be the wish of the two captains.

It is definitely not over yet, but India have a big mountain to climb. A win for England today means that they cannot lose this multi-format tour, as India can reach only upto 8 points, if they win the T20I series 3-0. The hosts have built up some really good momentum but the visitors did show some of their spark in the last game. The batting was looking to slowly come into its own, before folding up at the death while the bowling had England under the leash till the halfway mark of the chase. So the Indians too, are not far behind from churning out momentum.

It is time for the final game of this ODI series. In terms of status, this series is done, with England Women leading 2-0 but remember, this being a multi-format tour, series do not matter much. In spite of having lost this series, India can still end up winning the tour. How? if India win the next 4 games to come - 3 T20Is including this ODI, they end up with 10 points, which should put them in good stead. So you see, all is not over yet.
